lessons.title: Getting ready for a scheduled service
lessons.html:
What is a scheduled service?

A scheduled service is maintenance done at set engine hours, as written in the tractor's operator's manual. For example, there are daily checks, and then services at set hour intervals where oil, filters and other items are changed. Doing services on time keeps the tractor working in planting and harvest time, when a breakdown costs the farmer a lot of money.

Read the hour meter

Look at the hour meter on the dashboard. Write the hours on the job card. Check in the manual which service is due at those hours.

Get the right parts

  1. Look up the service kit or parts by tractor model and serial number.
  2. Collect the oil filter, fuel filters, air filter and any other parts.
  3. Check the oil types and amounts in the manual: engine oil, transmission and hydraulic oil, coolant, grease.
  4. Compare the new filters with the old ones before fitting.

Make the tractor safe

  • Park on level ground.
  • Lower the implements and loader.
  • Apply the handbrake and chock the wheels.
  • Stop the engine and take out the key.
  • Let very hot parts cool, but drain engine oil while warm so it flows well. Be careful: warm oil can still burn you.

Tools and equipment

Have ready: drip trays, filter wrench, spanners and sockets, grease gun, funnel, clean rags, absorbent, the used oil drum and filter bin. Wear overalls, safety boots, glasses and gloves.

Check before you start

Walk around the tractor. Look for leaks, damaged hoses, flat tyres, broken lights and loose parts. Write down what you see so the mechanic can check it.

lessons.title: Doing the service and finishing the job
lessons.html:
Service steps

Engine oil and filter

  1. Put the drip tray under the sump plug. Remove the plug and let the oil drain.
  2. Remove the oil filter with a filter wrench.
  3. Wipe the filter seat clean. Check the old seal came off.
  4. Put a little clean oil on the new filter seal. Screw on by hand as the filter says.
  5. Fit the sump plug with a new washer if needed and tighten as the manual says.
  6. Fill with the right oil and amount. Check the dipstick.

Fuel filters

Drain water from the water separator. Change the fuel filters as you were shown. Bleed air out of the fuel system if the manual says so. Clean up spilled diesel.

Air filter

Remove the outer element carefully so dust does not fall into the intake. Replace or clean it as the manual allows. Check the inner safety element but only change it when due. Check hoses and clamps.

Cooling system

Check the coolant level when the engine is cold. Blow out grass and chaff from the radiator and coolers. Check hoses and the fan belt.

Greasing

Grease every nipple on the lubrication chart. Wipe each nipple first. Pump until clean grease comes out. Report broken nipples.

Other checks

  • Transmission and hydraulic oil level
  • Battery terminals
  • Tyre pressures
  • Lights and warning lamps

Finishing the job

  1. Start the engine. Check the oil pressure light goes out.
  2. Look for leaks at the filters and plugs.
  3. Stop the engine, wait, check levels again.
  4. Put used oil in the drum and filters in the filter bin.
  5. Clean the area and your tools.
  6. Fill in the job card: hours, parts, oil amounts, problems found.
  7. Tell your mechanic or supervisor about anything you found.

Key points

  • Services are done by engine hours from the manual.
  • Use the right parts and oils for the tractor model.
  • Make the tractor safe before you start.
  • Check for leaks and levels after running the engine.
  • Record everything on the job card and recycle used oil and filters.
